desc: Easy White Bean Hummus (7 ingredients). Creamy, healthy, vegan, and gluten-free. Rich in plant-based protein, and lasts for up to 5 days.

title: White Bean Kale Salad
steps: Cook the quinoa according to the packet directions. Fluff with a fork. Set aside to cool.
Massage kale: Transfer the kale to a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt. Massage the kale for 1 minute, or until tender. Set aside.

Sauté beans: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté the butter beans for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the shallot and cook for 5 minutes more, stirring frequently. Add more oil as needed.
Add the garlic and walnuts and cook for another minute.
Season: Mix in the red wine vinegar, and maple syrup and cook for 2 minutes more. Remove from the heat. Season with salt and pepper.
Make dressing: Mix the tahini, lemon zest and juice, maple syrup, and hot water as needed to thin in a small bowl. Add salt to taste.
Combine: Transfer the bean mixture and quinoa to the bowl with the kale. Mix until fully incorporated. Season with salt and pepper.
Add dressing for serving.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

ing.text: 1 bunch kale ((lacinato or curly) thinly sliced)
1 to 2 tablespoons olive oil (plus more for drizzling (see notes for oil-free))
1 (15-ounce) can butter beans (or chickpeas or white beans, drained, and rinsed)
3 to 4 tablespoons lemon juice ((one medium lemon))

desc: This vegan White Bean Kale Salad is packed with plant-based protein. Plus, it's easy and healthy, with a creamy tahini dressing. Serve warm or…

title: White Bean Mushroom Stew with Potatoes
steps: Simmer tempeh (optional): Simmer the tempeh in water to cover by 2 inches for 3 minutes to remove the slightly bitter flavor before crumbling. Run the block under cold water. Use your hands to break the tempeh into crumbles.

Sauté tempeh: Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil over medium-high heat in a large nonstick skillet. Cook the tempeh crumbles, if using, for about 5 minutes until golden brown, stirring occasionally. Add 1 tablespoon soy sauce and cook for 1 minute more, stirring constantly. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Cook mushrooms: Add a drizzle of olive oil to the same skillet and heat over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for about 6 minutes, or until they release their liquid and brown, stirring occasionally. Transfer to the bowl with the tempeh, if using, and set aside.

Cook onion, carrots, and garlic: Drizzle more olive oil into the same skillet. Cook the onion, carrots, and garlic for about 5 minutes, or until the onions are translucent. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes more, stirring constantly.
Add liquid: Whisk in the vegetable broth and lemon juice.

Add the potatoes, bay leaves, rosemary, thyme, oregano, and basil. Bring the liquid to a gentle boil before reducing the heat to a low simmer. Simmer with the lid on for about 15 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork tender, stirring occasionally, and adding more broth as needed to keep the vegetables submerged.

Combine ingredients and season: Discard the bay leaves. Add the tempeh crumbles (if using), beans, peas, and coconut milk. Add more water or broth as needed until the desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust soy sauce and lemon juice to taste.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

ing.text: 2 teaspoons olive oil (plus more as needed (optional))
2 tablespoons soy sauce (or tamari (divided), plus more as needed)
16 ounces cremini mushrooms (or white button, quartered)
½ cup wholewheat pastry flour (or all-purpose)
2 tablespoons lemon juice (plus more as needed)
15 ounces cannellini beans (or navy, or Great Northern, canned with liquid)
1 1/3 cups unsweetened coconut milk (canned, or unsweetened nondairy milk)

title: White Bean Soup with Quinoa Recipe
steps: Mirepoix: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion, carrots, and celery for about 5 minutes, or until the onion is translucent. Add the zucchini and cook for one more minute.
Herbs & spices: Mix in the garlic, smoked paprika, thyme, crushed red pepper, and chipotle. Cook for another minute, stirring constantly.

Liquids & quinoa: Add the vegetable broth, 2 cups water, quinoa, diced tomatoes, and bay leaves. Simmer partially covered for about 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is cooked. Add more broth as desired.
Season: Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the white beans, kale, and nutritional yeast. Cook until the kale is just wilted. Season with fresh lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

Salt and freshly ground black pepper (to taste)

title: White Bean Tostadas Recipe
steps: Make tostadas (optional): To make homemade tostadas, place corn tortillas on a baking sheet and lightly brush or spray both sides with oil. Place a second baking sheet directly on top to help keep the tortillas flat while baking.Bake at 400°F for about 12 to 15 minutes, or until crisp and golden. Flip halfway if needed.

Prep the ingredients: Dice the red onion, grate the garlic, cut the avocado into pieces, and drain and rinse the beans well if using canned beans.If you prefer a milder onion flavor, soak the diced onion in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes before using.
Combine: Add the avocado, white beans, red onion, sriracha, nutritional yeast, garlic, lime juice, lime zest, salt, and black pepper to a large bowl. Add olive oil of using.

Smash the mixture: Use a potato masher, pizza cutter, or large fork to partially smash the mixture until creamy but still textured.For a smoother white bean mash, pulse everything a few times in a food processor. Avoid blending too much or the mixture can become overly smooth and dense.Keeping the mixture slightly chunky instead of fully puréed may also help slow digestion because more of the bean structure remains intact.
Assemble: Spread the white bean mash onto the tostadas and top with sprouts, herbs, avocado, or extra lime juice if desired.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

Salt and freshly ground black pepper (to taste)

title: White Beans in Cauliflower Cream Sauce Recipe
steps: Cut the Cauliflower. Cut the cauliflower into evenly sized, medium-sized florets so they steam at the same rate.

Steam the Cauliflower. Steam for about 10 to 12 minutes, until very tender—it should mash easily with a fork. Optional: Add the garlic during the final 5 minutes to mellow its flavor. Drain well so excess water doesn’t thin the cauliflower cream sauce.

Blend the Cauliflower Cream Sauce. Transfer the cauliflower and garlic to a blender. Add the artichoke hearts, nutritional yeast, mustard, onion powder, black pepper, and nondairy milk or broth. Blend until completely smooth, adding more liquid only as needed for a thick but pourable sauce.
Warm the Cauliflower Cream Sauce. Pour the blended sauce into a large skillet and warm over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally.
Add the White Beans. Gently fold the beans into the warm sauce and cook for about 5 to 7 minutes, until heated through. Add a splash of water or broth if needed to loosen the sauce.
Dissolve the Miso. In a small bowl, stir the miso with the water until smooth.

Finish Off the Heat. Remove the skillet from the stove and let cool slightly. Stir in the fresh herbs, lemon zest, lemon juice, and dissolved miso to taste. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Serve with a sprinkle of fresh herbs.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

½ cup unsweetened nondairy milk ( or vegetable broth, plus more as needed)

title: Why I Always Keep Ground Tofu In My Fridge
steps: Press tofu if using firm, pat dry, then crumble into small pieces.
Mix together the seasonings and pour over the crumbled tofu.
Oven method: Preheat to 180°C fan (350°F). Spread on a tray and bake for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and chewy.
Air fryer method: Cook at 190°C (375°F) for 12–15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Pan-fry method: Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add the tofu and cook for 10–15 minutes, turning regularly.
Plant-based Arayes
Serves: 3–4
Ingredients
batch prepared ground tofu (made with 450g tofu)
ml hot vegetable stock, as needed
small onion, very finely diced or grated
garlic cloves, minced
tsp ground cumin
tsp ground coriander
½ tsp smoked paprika
¼ tsp dried mint
¼ tsp ground allspice
tsp harissa paste
tbsp pomegranate molasses
tbsp tomato purée
g fresh parsley, finely chopped
g fresh coriander, finely chopped
Zest of half a lemon
tbsp potato starch
pita breads
Olive oil, for brushing
For the whipped tahini
g tahini
small garlic clove, finely grated
tbsp lemon juice
ml ice-cold water, as needed
½ tsp ground cumin, optional
tbsp zaatar seasoning
Method

Place the prepared ground tofu in a bowl and add the finely diced onion, crushed garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, mint, allspice, harissa, pomegranate molasses, tomato purée, parsley, coriander, potato starch and lemon juice. Mix thoroughly until everything is evenly combined.
Gradually mix in the hot water, a little at a time, until the tofu softens and becomes moist but not wet. Leave for 5 minutes to absorb the liquid. You may not need all the water.
Carefully cut a pocket into the side of each pita bread. Divide the filling between the pitas, spreading it into an even layer without overfilling. Press gently to compact the filling.

To make the whipped tahini, whisk the tahini, garlic and lemon juice together in a bowl. The mixture will thicken at first. Gradually whisk in the ice-cold water, a little at a time, until it becomes pale, smooth and fluffy. Stir in the cumin, if using, and adjust the lemon or water to taste. It will thicken in the fridge.

Air fryer method: Preheat to 170°C (340°F). Brush both sides of each stuffed pita lightly with olive oil and arrange in the air fryer basket. Cook for 15–20 minutes, turning halfway through, until the bread is crisp and golden and the filling is piping hot.

Oven method: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F / 180°C fan). Brush both sides of each stuffed pita lightly with olive oil and arrange on a baking tray. Bake for 12–18 minutes, turning halfway through, until the bread is crisp and golden and the filling is piping hot. If needed, finish under the grill for a minute or two to get extra colour, keeping a close eye on them.
Cut the arayes into halves or wedges and serve hot with the whipped tahini topped with zaatar.

title: Why Would a Chef Stop Eating Meat, Fish & Dairy?
steps: Bring the water, salt and dark soy sauce to a gentle simmer. Add the tofu and oyster mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain very well and leave to steam dry for a few minutes. Pat dry if necessary.

Mix the marinade ingredients together. Add the tofu and mushrooms and very gently toss until thoroughly coated, taking care not to break the tofu. Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably a few hours. If there is any excess marinade, brush it over the tofu and mushrooms as they marinate.
Thread the tofu and mushrooms onto skewers, alternating between them. If using wooden skewers, soak them beforehand.
Cook the Kebabs:

Air fryer: Arrange the skewers in the air fryer basket, leaving a little space between them. Air fry at 200°C / 400°F for 10–14 minutes, turning halfway, until deeply coloured and slightly crisp around the edges.

Oven grill: Place the skewers on a lined baking tray and cook under a very hot grill until deeply charred and golden, turning once or twice during cooking. Keep an eye on them as the yoghurt marinade can colour quickly.
If cooking on a barbecue or in a hot frying/grill pan, tear or cut the tofu into larger chunks instead, which will be easier to handle.
Lime & Coconut Cavolo Nero
Ingredients
g (14 oz) cavolo nero
g (½ cup) desiccated coconut
g (⅓ oz) fresh ginger, finely grated
tsp olive oil
Juice of 1 lime
Method

Remove the tough stems from the cavolo nero and roughly chop the leaves. Place in a large heatproof bowl and pour over enough boiling salted water to completely cover. Leave until the water has cooled, allowing the cavolo nero to soften while retaining its vibrant colour.
Meanwhile, heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the desiccated coconut to the dry pan and toast for 1–2 minutes, stirring frequently, until lightly golden.
Add the finely grated ginger and cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Drain the cavolo nero very well, squeezing out any excess water if necessary. Add a drizzle of olive oil to the pan, followed by the drained cavolo nero.
Toss over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, allowing any remaining excess water to evaporate and the cavolo nero to pick up the toasted coconut and ginger.
Remove from the heat and add the lime juice. Season with salt, toss well and serve.
Fluffy Basmati Rice
Ingredients
g (2 cups) basmati rice
ml (2⅓–2½ cups) water
cardamom pods, bashed
cloves
tsp nigella/onion seeds
½ tsp salt
Method
Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Add the rice, water, cardamom, cloves, nigella/onion seeds and salt to a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 10–12 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for another 10 minutes.
Remove the cardamom pods and cloves if you like, then fluff the rice gently with a fork.
Tangy Coriander Chutney
Ingredients
½ tbsp vegan Greek-style yoghurt
g (¾ oz) fresh coriander
Juice of ½ lemon or lime
½ tsp chaat masala
⅛ tsp ground cumin
¼ tsp sugar or maple syrup
A small pinch of chilli powder
small ice cubes
Method
Add everything to a blender and blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.

title: Zucchini Lasagna Recipe
steps: Marinate tofu: Slice the tofu thinly into about 16 equal-sized rectangles, approximately 1/4-inch-thick. Mix the tamari, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, and water in a large rimmed baking dish. Place the tofu slices in the marinade in a single layer. Set aside for at least 20 minutes, or overnight, flipping them over after 10 minutes.
Soak cashews: Bring the cashews to a boil in a saucepan with water to cover. Remove from the heat and set aside to soak for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375ºF.

Make vegan ricotta: Drain the cashews. Place them in a blender with the apple cider vinegar, nutritional yeast, onion powder, garlic, parsley, and water. Blend on high until smooth. Add more water as needed until a spreadable texture. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Make the sauce: Mix the cooked lentils with the marinara sauce and chopped spinach.

Layer: Add about one-third of the lentil sauce mixture to the bottom of a 9x13 lasagna pan or rectangular medium-large casserole dish. Place about one-third of the marinated tofu slices in a single layer on top of the lentil sauce. Layer with sliced zucchini to cover. Add about one-third of the ricotta in dollops using a spoon. Spread it in an even layer on top of the zucchini. Add about one-third more marinara lentil mixture. Spread in an even layer. Add about one-third of the tofu in a single layer. Layer sliced zucchini on top to cover. Top the zucchini with one-third of the ricotta in dollops. Spread it in an even layer. Add the remaining lentil sauce over the top. Add the remaining tofu in a single layer. Add zucchini to cover. Top with the remaining ricotta in dollops. Spread evenly over the top. Add a sprinkle of hemp hearts, as desired.
Bake for about 25 minutes, or until warmed through. Optional: Broil for 2 minutes more to brown the top.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN

title: Zucchini Scallion Pancakes Recipe
steps: Soak the lentils: Rinse the red lentils well. Cover generously with water and soak for 3 hours. Drain and rinse thoroughly. Leave them in the strainer for several minutes to remove as much excess water as possible. Do not cook the lentils.

Prepare the zucchini: Cut the zucchini into long, thin matchsticks using a julienne peeler or mandoline, or cut it lengthwise with a sharp chef's knife to create long julienne strands. Alternatively, use the large holes of a box grater to shred the zucchini into long strands, grating lengthwise when possible.Salt the zucchini: Place the zucchini in a large bowl, sprinkle with ½ teaspoon salt, and toss well with your hands to evenly coat the strands. Let stand for at least 10 minutes to draw out excess moisture. Squeeze well: Transfer the zucchini to a clean kitchen towel, then use your hands to wring out and squeeze firmly to remove as much liquid as possible. Separate the strands with your fingers.

Make the lentil batter: Add the drained lentils, soy milk, tamari, rice vinegar, optional sesame oil, ginger, garlic, baking powder, baking soda, salt and black pepper (if using) to a high-speed blender. Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.Transfer the batter: Pour the red lentil batter into a large, clean bowl.

Add the vegetables: Add the squeezed zucchini, scallions, red onion, and optional red pepper flakes to the batter. Toss well until evenly coated. The mixture should look predominantly like vegetables, not batter. There should be just enough batter surrounding the strands to hold them together.

Heat the skillet: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium to medium-low heat. Lightly brush with oil, if using. Add the sesame seeds: Sprinkle about 1 1/2 teaspoons sesame seeds directly onto the skillet where each pancake will go.

Form the pancakes: Immediately add about 3/4 cup of the zucchini mixture directly over the sesame seeds. Use a spatula to spread and press it into a thin round. Keep the vegetables packed together so the pancake holds when flipped.
Cook: Cook for 4 to 5 minutes on the first side, or until deeply golden underneath, crisp around the edges, and sufficiently set to flip without falling apart.

Flip carefully: Slide a wide spatula completely underneath the pancake and flip. Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes, pressing gently with the spatula, until golden and cooked through. Reduce the heat if the exterior is browning before the center sets.
Repeat with the remaining mixture and sesame seeds, adding more oil as needed.
Cut: Let the pancakes cool slightly to firm up, then use a sharp knife to cut them into squares.
Serve: Serve warm and crispy with my Creamy Asian Tahini Dressing for dipping or drizzling.
author: Nisha Melvani, RDN
